segments.text: Hello, I'm Daisy, a Cloud Support  Engineer here at the AWS office in
Sydney. I'm going to show you how  to add tags to your AWS resources
to separate the entries in your bill by  cost center or project. Let's get started.
Tags are key and value pairs that can help you  organize your AWS resources into groups. Tags
can help you manage, identify, and search for  and filter your AWS resources. When you apply
tags to your resources, you can see the tagged  resources all in one place as resource groups.
You can also use Cost Explorer  and Cost and Usage Reports to
view billing information about your  tagged resources. And you can use
AWS Budgets to send notifications about  spending limits related to specific tags.
After logging in to the AWS Management Console,  navigate to the Tag Editor console. For Regions,
select all the Regions that  apply. For resource types,
select the required resources. Leave the  tags field empty for now. Choose Search
resources. The results are visible  at the bottom half of the page.
For my example, I want to add  tags with keys such as Project,
CostCenter, and Environment. Choose the top  check box to select all the visible resources,
and then choose Manage tags of selected resources.  Now choose Add tag to start adding the tag keys.
Note that tag keys and values are case sensitive.  Choose Add tag, and enter CostCenter. Choose Add
tag, and enter Environment. Choose Review and  apply tag changes. After you review the changes,
choose Apply changes to all selected. Choose  Search resources to get the result again.
Now let's add values to these keys to help
organize the resources. There  are a couple of ways to do this,
depending on whether you want to add the same  values to multiple resources or to just a few.
To add values to multiple resources at the same  time, choose the individual check boxes to select
the required resources, and then choose Manage  tags of selected resources. Enter the value in
the Tag value column. Note that if the Tag value  column presents a dropdown list with options,
you can still enter a new value. However, your  new value will replace the key's existing values
for that resource. Choose Review and apply  tag changes. After you review the changes,
choose Apply changes to all selected. Choose  Search resources to get the result again.
If you want to add unique tag values for  individual resources, choose Preferences,
which is the gear icon on the right side of the  search results. Turn on the required tag keys by
using the toggle buttons. Choose Confirm. Your tag  key now appear as columns in the search results
table. Locate the tag key for the resource  and choose the field to edit each tag value.
So now you know how to add tags to your AWS  resources to separate the entries in your bill by
cost center or project. Thanks for watching, and  happy cloud computing from all of us here at AWS.
